name: Critical minerals
summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause ends on 10 Nov; no legal renewal found as of 8 Nov
state: China's one-year pause on its October 2025 rare-earth export controls ends on 10 Nov (Mining Technology). China's commerce ministry said on 28 Sep that the wider trade arrangement runs to 10 Jan 2027, but the notice had not been amended as of 27 Oct (Materials Dispatch), and searches on 8 Nov found no renewal. April 2025 licensing for seven rare earths remains in force (Mining Technology). No production stoppages outside China were found, so the Alert line is not crossed.
for_you: Makers of electric vehicles, wind turbines, electronics and defence equipment rely on Chinese rare-earth supply and are exposed to tighter licensing, including longer waits for permits.
rubric_hit: Licensing in force and pause expiring 10 Nov (Watch line); no reported production stoppages outside China for Alert

sources.title: Materials Dispatch — China's November 2026 Export-Control Cliff
Mining Technology via Yahoo Finance — China rare earth export pause nears expiry

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
